question.html:
A truck is traveling along a straight, horizontal road at a constant horizontal velocity of 24 m s.

a. On the diagram below, draw and label all vertical forces that act on the truck.

  [2]

b. Explain why the velocity of the truck is constant. In your explanation, refer to Newton’s laws of motion.

  [2]

c. The total horizontal resistive force that acts on the truck is 5.4 kN. The efficiency of the truck’s engine is 28%. Calculate the total power produced by the truck’s engine. 

  [3]

d. State one reason why not all the power that you calculated in part (c) is used to keep the truck moving at a constant speed.

  [1]

e. The truck’s engine is switched off and the truck slows down without applying its breaks. It takes the truck 21.5 seconds to reach a velocity of 10 m s. Assuming that the resistive force acting on the truck is constant, calculate the mass of the truck.

  [2]

f. Based on another assumption, the total resistive force consists of two components: a constant frictional force of 1.2 kN and a second component that is proportional to the square of the truck’s velocity.

i. State the magnitude of the second component when the truck’s velocity is 24 m s.

  [1]

ii. Calculate the total horizontal resistive force when the truck’s velocity is 12 m s.

  [3]
